answer: Time-locked bandwidth quotas. Each identity may send only as many messages as its measured historical latency budget allows, enforced by relay logs. A ripple of prior activity earns the next send slot; new identities wait in a queue while the wharf drains one message per cooldown. An attacker must rent real relay capacity across an ocean of distinct IPs and hold it idle through the full wait, paying hosting and delay costs per fake identity rather than a one-time fee.
